description: Runnable templates for C# values, branching, iteration, functions, types, patterns, nullability, and asynchronous flow.
executionSupportMessage: Compatible with the built-in .NET 10 C# runner; authored against .NET 8.

actionDescriptions.Access: Retrieves a value exposed through a language or runtime feature without intentionally changing it.
actionDescriptions.Create: Constructs a new object, resource, or language structure.
actionDescriptions.Enumerate: Traverses a sequence of values or members one item at a time.
actionDescriptions.Protect: Applies a security-sensitive transformation or comparison.
actionDescriptions.Run: Starts work and waits for or observes its outcome.
actionDescriptions.Select: Chooses one branch, value, or subset from the available alternatives.
actionDescriptions.Slice: Creates a bounded view over part of an existing value or memory region.
actionDescriptions.Test: Evaluates a condition and returns whether it is satisfied.
actionDescriptions.Transform: Produces a new value by applying a language or library operation.
actionDescriptions.Wait: Asynchronously or synchronously pauses until a condition is met.

objectDescriptions.Alternative: An alternative is one of two mutually exclusive statement branches selected by a Boolean condition.
objectDescriptions.Awaitable operation: An awaitable operation exposes a completion protocol that C# can suspend for without blocking the current thread.
objectDescriptions.Branch: A branch is a block of statements whose execution depends on a condition.
objectDescriptions.Collection: A collection stores a sequence or set of values under one strongly typed object.
objectDescriptions.Constant: A constant is a named value fixed at compile time and unavailable for later assignment.
objectDescriptions.Conditional loop: A conditional loop repeats while a Boolean condition remains true.
objectDescriptions.Counted loop: A counted loop exposes explicit initialization, continuation, and update expressions.
objectDescriptions.Disposable resource: A disposable resource owns cleanup-sensitive state such as a file handle, stream, lock, or native object.
objectDescriptions.Fallback value: A fallback value substitutes for a nullable expression only when that expression is null.
objectDescriptions.Lambda: A lambda is an anonymous function that can be converted to a delegate or expression tree.
objectDescriptions.Local function: A local function is a named function declared inside another member or a top-level program.
objectDescriptions.Nullable member: A nullable member access may produce no result when its receiver is null.
objectDescriptions.Operation: An operation is a block of work that may complete normally or raise an exception.
objectDescriptions.Property pattern: A property pattern tests an object's type, shape, and nested property values.
objectDescriptions.Range: A range identifies a contiguous, end-exclusive portion of a range-capable value.
objectDescriptions.Record: A record is a data-focused C# type with synthesized value equality and nondestructive mutation support.
objectDescriptions.Sequence: A sequence exposes values one at a time through C# enumeration.
objectDescriptions.Switch expression: A switch expression maps an input value to an output by testing ordered patterns.
objectDescriptions.Tuple: A value tuple groups a fixed number of strongly typed elements without requiring a dedicated type declaration.
objectDescriptions.Variable: A variable is a named, strongly typed storage location whose value can be read and usually reassigned.

commands.name: Language.Variable
commands.description: Declare a local variable whose type is inferred.
commands.definition: The var keyword asks the compiler to infer the local variable's static type from its initializer. The variable remains strongly typed; var is not a dynamic value.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The expression used to initialize the variable.

examples.title: Infer a string variable
examples.code:
var projectName = "Hypershell";
Console.WriteLine(projectName);
examples.explanation: The compiler infers string from the initializer while retaining compile-time type checking.

commands.name: Language.Constant
commands.description: Declare a compile-time constant.
commands.definition: A const local or field must be initialized with a compile-time constant expression and cannot be assigned again. Constants are appropriate for values that are truly fixed by the program.

examples.title: Define a retry limit
examples.code:
const int MaxAttempts = 3;
Console.WriteLine($"Retry limit: {MaxAttempts}");
examples.explanation: MaxAttempts is embedded as a compile-time constant and cannot be reassigned.

commands.name: Language.If
commands.description: Run a block only when a condition is true.
commands.definition: An if statement evaluates a Boolean expression and executes its body only when that expression is true.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: One or more statements to run when the condition is true.

examples.title: Validate a file before reading
examples.explanation: The file is opened only when the existence check succeeds.

commands.name: Language.IfElse
commands.description: Choose between two statement blocks.
commands.definition: An if-else statement runs exactly one of two branches according to the result of a Boolean condition.

examples.title: Report an input result
examples.explanation: TryParse controls which branch runs without throwing for invalid input.

commands.name: Language.SwitchExpression
commands.description: Map one input value to one result expression.
commands.definition: A switch expression compares an input against ordered patterns and returns the expression associated with the first matching arm. A discard arm commonly supplies the fallback.

parameters.name: arms
parameters.description: Comma-separated pattern arms, including a fallback when needed.

examples.title: Classify an HTTP status
examples.explanation: Relational and logical patterns turn a numeric status into a descriptive category.

commands.name: Language.ForEach
commands.description: Run a block once for each value in a sequence.
commands.definition: A foreach statement obtains an enumerator from a sequence and executes its body for each element. It is the usual loop for IEnumerable<T> values.

parameters.name: itemName
parameters.description: The identifier for the current element.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Statements to run for each element.

examples.title: Print normalized names
examples.explanation: The loop visits each array element in order and works with one strongly typed value at a time.

commands.name: Language.For
commands.description: Repeat a block with explicit initialization, condition, and update.
commands.definition: A for statement combines loop initialization, a continuation condition, and an iterator expression. It is useful when an index or exact iteration count matters.

parameters.name: initializer
parameters.description: The loop initializer, such as int index = 0.

parameters.name: iterator
parameters.description: The update performed after each iteration.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Statements to run in each iteration.

examples.title: Print valid list indexes
examples.explanation: The condition keeps every array access within the valid zero-based index range.

commands.name: Language.While
commands.description: Repeat a block while a condition remains true.
commands.definition: A while statement checks its Boolean condition before each iteration. Its body may execute zero times when the initial condition is false.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Statements that make progress toward ending the loop.

examples.title: Process a queue
examples.explanation: TryDequeue both tests for an item and removes it, so the loop ends when the queue is empty.

commands.name: Language.TryCatch
commands.description: Handle a selected exception from a protected block.
commands.definition: A try statement runs protected code. A matching catch clause handles an exception, and an optional finally clause performs cleanup regardless of success or failure.

parameters.name: handler
parameters.description: Statements that respond to the exception.

examples.title: Handle malformed JSON
examples.explanation: Only JSON parsing failures are caught; unrelated exceptions are not silently swallowed.

commands.name: Language.UsingDeclaration
commands.description: Dispose a resource automatically when its scope ends.
commands.definition: A using declaration registers an IDisposable or IAsyncDisposable value for deterministic cleanup at the end of the current scope, including when an exception leaves that scope.

parameters.name: resource
parameters.description: An expression returning an IDisposable value.

examples.title: Close a file stream reliably
examples.code:
using var stream = File.OpenRead("input.bin");
Console.WriteLine($"Length: {stream.Length:N0} bytes");
examples.explanation: The stream is disposed automatically when the enclosing top-level scope completes.

commands.name: Language.LocalFunction
commands.description: Declare a named function inside the current member or top-level program.
commands.definition: A local function packages reusable logic within its containing scope. It can capture surrounding variables and can be generic, recursive, asynchronous, or an iterator.

examples.title: Normalize a reusable label
examples.explanation: The helper stays scoped to this program and can be called like any other strongly typed method.

commands.name: Language.Lambda
commands.description: Create an inline anonymous function.
commands.definition: A lambda expression creates a delegate or expression-tree value from parameters and an expression or statement body. Lambdas can capture variables from the enclosing scope.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: The expression returned by the lambda.

examples.title: Create a reusable predicate
examples.explanation: The lambda is converted to Func<string, bool> and can be passed to filtering APIs.

commands.name: Language.Tuple
commands.description: Group several named values without declaring a dedicated type.
commands.definition: A value tuple stores a fixed number of strongly typed elements. Element names improve readability but do not change the tuple's runtime type identity.

examples.title: Return a compact result
examples.code:
var result = (Files: 12, Errors: 1);
Console.WriteLine($"Files={result.Files}; Errors={result.Errors}");
examples.explanation: Named elements make the two integer values self-describing without a separate class.

commands.name: Language.Record
commands.description: Declare an immutable-oriented data type with value equality.
commands.definition: A record is a reference or value type designed for data models. Positional records synthesize properties, value equality, deconstruction, and a readable string representation.

examples.title: Model an immutable project
examples.explanation: The with expression creates a copy with one changed property while value-based formatting displays both fields.

commands.name: Language.PropertyPattern
commands.description: Test an object's shape and property values.
commands.definition: A property pattern recursively matches accessible properties and can introduce a typed variable when the input satisfies the requested shape.

examples.title: Recognize a successful response shape
examples.explanation: The property pattern tests the status range without separately extracting StatusCode.

commands.name: Language.CollectionExpression
commands.description: Create a collection using compact bracket syntax.
commands.definition: A collection expression uses bracket syntax and optional spread elements to initialize a compatible collection type. The target type determines the resulting representation.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: Comma-separated elements and optional spread elements.

examples.title: Combine fixed and spread elements
examples.explanation: The spread element inserts every value from core between the fixed first and last entries.

commands.name: Language.NullCoalescing
commands.description: Use a fallback when a nullable value is null.
commands.definition: The null-coalescing operator returns its left operand when non-null and otherwise evaluates and returns its right operand. The right side is not evaluated unnecessarily.

parameters.name: fallback
parameters.description: The value used only when the left side is null.

examples.title: Default a missing environment value
examples.explanation: Production is used only when APP_MODE is absent, not when it contains an empty string.

commands.name: Language.NullConditional
commands.description: Access a member only when its receiver is non-null.
commands.definition: The null-conditional operator short-circuits member or element access when the receiver is null and produces null instead of throwing NullReferenceException.

parameters.name: member
parameters.description: The member access or invocation after ?..

examples.title: Read an optional string length
examples.explanation: The chained calls are skipped when label is null, and the nullable length remains null.

commands.name: Language.RangeSlice
commands.description: Select a contiguous range by index.
commands.definition: Range and index expressions describe a start and end boundary. The end is exclusive, and the ^ operator counts backward from the end of the sequence.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: A range-capable value such as a string or array.

examples.title: Remove the first and last characters
examples.explanation: Index 1 skips the opening bracket and ^1 identifies the position immediately before the final bracket.

commands.name: Language.Await
commands.description: Asynchronously wait for an operation without blocking its thread.
commands.definition: The await operator suspends the current asynchronous flow until its awaitable completes, then retrieves the result or propagates its exception.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description: A Task<T>, ValueTask<T>, or other awaitable expression.

examples.title: Await asynchronous file I/O
examples.code:
var text = await File.ReadAllTextAsync("README.md");
Console.WriteLine($"Characters: {text.Length:N0}");
examples.explanation: The generated top-level C# program supports await directly and resumes with the file contents.
